name: Korean BBQ Chicken Wings
desc: Grilled chicken wings marinated in gochujang, soy sauce, brown sugar, and ginger, then brushed with the boiled marinade.

source.title: Crispy Korean BBQ Chicken Wings
source.evidence: All twelve ingredients and amounts match this page, as do the 1 hour marinade, 400°F grill, and boiled-marinade glaze.

ingredients.raw: 4 lb chicken wings, split into drumettes and flats
1/3 cup gochujang (Korean red chili pepper paste)
1 1/2 tbsp fresh ginger, peeled and minced
1 tsp toasted sesame seeds, for garnish
2 green onions, thinly sliced, for garnish

steps: Put the wings in a large zip-top bag.
Whisk the gochujang, brown sugar, soy sauce, water, sesame oil, vinegar, garlic, ginger, salt, and pepper in a small bowl until smooth. Pour over the wings, seal, and refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Preheat the grill to 400°F. Lift the wings out of the bag and pour the marinade into a small saucepan; keep it for the glaze.
Grill the wings, flipping every 10-15 min, until the skin is crisp and the thickest drumette reads 165°F, 30-40 min total. Move to a plate.
Bring the reserved marinade to a full boil over high heat and boil, stirring constantly, 1-2 min (this makes the raw-chicken marinade safe to use).
Brush the wings with the glaze, sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onion, and serve right away.
tips: Wings are safe at 165°F but render and crisp better if you keep going to 175-185°F; they stay juicy.
